overview: This study note examines the reasons why Israel rejected the message, the remedy for that rejection, and the resulting consequences of their rejection. It explores the dynamics between their relationship with God, the law, and the need for belief.

topics.title: Reasons for Rejection
topics.summary: Israel rejected the message due to a lack of feeling the need for salvation, being zealous for God while making their own traditions, and being proud and self-righteous, along with misunderstanding their own law.
key_points: Did not feel need for salvation; thought they were fine, save themselves.
Zealous for God; made own traditions and worshipped them.
Proud and self-righteous; refused to listen and learn.
Misunderstood their own law; the law leads the sinner to the savior, and must be obeyed in the heart.

topics.title: Remedy for Rejection
topics.summary: The remedy for rejection involves using a missionary program and understanding that believing and obeying are not interchangeable, emphasizing that one must first hear.
key_points: To believe one must first hear.

topics.title: Results of Rejection
topics.summary: The rejection of Israel results in Israel being guilty, the message being shared with Gentiles, and God still yearning for His people.
key_points: Israel is guilty; Israel DID hear.
Message is shared with Gentiles due to Israel rejection.
God still yearns for His people.
